searchText: <cskiraly> re: **@fede_intern** > you can use neon but not as powerful. didn’t see any blake implementation using it but might be interesting to do so For enabling Neon support, I've found this to be quite useful: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/102581/0200/Port-with-SSE2Neon-and-SIMDe Used it here (in a different context, for SSE2 in RS): https://github.com/catid/leopard/pull/19 <chfast> Can I get access to the dashboard? <parithoshj> re: **@chfast** > Can I get access to the dashboard? dm-ing <chfast> Catching with the recent date, even after modexp repricing there are still cases running at ~30mgps in Go. I've checked the FastExp in Erigon, but this is the same strategy as Go has been doing since 1.20. Any ideas how to solve this for Erigon/Geth? What kind of inputs are these? We have investigated this a bit last week, and the main issue is the following: Go stdlib has two paths for exp: a naive path which is squaring and dividing, and an optimized path with montgomery multiplication. The montgomery based path is taken for exponent > 64bit, and it's actually kind of OK performance wise So we tried to lower the threshold for entering the montgomery based path down to size of 8 bits and it seems like it still performs a bit better <chfast> The modexp repricing EIP makes all values at least 32-byte long, so the small numbers are not a concern any more. So the top ones are the slowest? Can we get them as statetests? I don't know where to find these inputs, we need them as standalone statetest in order to work with them. For modexp imputs we could be synced with EEST at https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/main/tests/zkevm/test_worst_compute.py#L804, but this is not in my direct control. could be synced? do you know which cases there correspond to your 'ModexPawel4' case? ahh, nvm, I found it <marcin_d_s> these are the most interesting cases (ignore Expected): { "Input": "", "Expected": "00", "Name": "pawel-4-exp-heavy", "Gas": 506, "NoBenchmark": false }, { "Input": "", "Expected": "00", "Name": "pawel-5-mod-even-32b-exp-40", "Gas": 208, "NoBenchmark": false }, { "Input": "", "Expected": "00", "Name": "pawel-6-mod-even-32b-exp-256", "Gas": 1360, "NoBenchmark": false } These should be already included in https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/benchmark%40v0.0.2

excerpts.content: <chfast> Catching with the recent date, even after modexp repricing there are still cases running at ~30mgps in Go. I've checked the FastExp in Erigon, but this is the same strategy as Go has been doing since 1.20. Any ideas how to solve this for Erigon/Geth?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: We have investigated this a bit last week, and the main issue is the following:

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: Go stdlib has two paths for exp: a naive path which is squaring and dividing, and an optimized path with montgomery multiplication.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The montgomery based path is taken for exponent > 64bit, and it's actually kind of OK performance wise

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: So we tried to lower the threshold for entering the montgomery based path down to size of 8 bits and it seems like it still performs a bit better
